resources.string: Your data stays on your phone.
Every app you watch lives here as a little creature. It grows when its app talks to the internet, and grows faster when it meets trackers. Tap a creature to see what it has been up to.
Pick the apps Mycelium should watch. Only these apps go through Mycelium; all other apps are left alone. You can change this any time.
A live list of what your watched apps did. Most entries are lookups: an app asking where a website lives. Mycelium sees the name of the website, never what is sent.
Garden shows each app with the trackers it met, and lets you block them. Charts show totals and how activity changed over time.
Ask questions in plain words. The Gardener answers from what this phone has seen, and every sentence links to the events it is based on. It works offline and never makes things up.
A checklist of phone settings that help Mycelium see clearly and keep running. Tap Fix to jump to the right setting.
Change the look, add your own AI key, or turn on advanced tools.
Short explanations of every word Mycelium uses.
What stays on your phone, what can leave it, and who made the parts of this app.
Tools for curious people and developers: ask the database directly, export or wipe it, run a demo, and see technical details.
Mycelium is watching %1$s. Everything it notices stays on this phone.
Mycelium is resting. Your apps work normally, but nothing is recorded.
No internet right now. Mycelium answers your apps on the phone and sends nothing. It sorts what it caught when you are back online.
Protection stopped unexpectedly. Try starting it again.
A demo with made-up apps is playing. Stop it to see your real garden.
Android needs your OK before protection can start.
Pick at least one app to watch first.
Protected: Mycelium is watching your chosen apps. Paused: it is off and records nothing. Safe Mode: there is no internet, so it answers apps on the phone and sorts what it caught later.
Start protection to see what your apps do.
Pick the apps you want to watch. Each one gets a little creature that grows when the app talks to the internet.
You\'re offline. Mycelium is holding on to what it catches.
Apps that came with your phone, like the dialer or settings. They are hidden to keep the list short; apps you already watch are always shown.
No downloaded apps found. Turn on Show system apps to see the ones that came with your phone.
Each watched app gets a creature. It is just for fun: every creature grows the same way. You can change it later in Insights.
Start protection and open one of your watched apps. Each time it looks up a website, it appears here.
Android told us which app asked.
Android told us which app connected.
Best guess: the app that was on screen.
We could not tell which app.
Usually Android tells Mycelium exactly which app asked. When it can\'t, Mycelium guesses the app that was on screen, and says so.
Choose apps to watch and they will show up here with everything they did today.
Growth is points earned from the app\'s activity: each lookup counts 1, a tracker lookup counts 2. At enough points the creature reaches the next stage.
Companies that collect data about you, like ad and analytics networks. Block one to stop this app from reaching it. The app may lose an ad or a feature, but usually keeps working.
How much data the app sent and received, counted by Android. Android adds it up in blocks of about two hours, so the newest use appears a little later.
Unusual behaviour, for example many new websites at once, activity in the middle of the night, or a first contact with a tracker company.
No data for this period yet.
A lookup is an app asking \"where does this website live?\". It happens before almost everything an app does online, so it is a good sign of activity.
On screen: you were using the app. Background: the app was active while you were not looking at it.
Your watched apps ranked by what you pick: lookups, tracker lookups, data, or background activity.
Deletes all questions and answers. Your data and stats stay.

Optional. With your own key and internet, a cloud AI can phrase the answer. Before anything is sent you see exactly what will go out, and nothing leaves until you tap Send. Without it, the Gardener answers on your phone.
Ask AI needs your own key (Settings) and an internet connection. Answers come from this phone only.

Android may stop Mycelium to save battery. Allow unrestricted battery use.
Chrome can hide its lookups. In Chrome open Settings, Privacy and security, and turn Use secure DNS off.
Open app info and set Autostart on, Battery saver to No restrictions, and Pause app activity if unused off.
A phone setting that sends lookups straight to a chosen company, around Mycelium. When it names a provider, Mycelium sees nothing. Off or Automatic is fine.
Auto follows your phone\'s dark mode. Day is warm paper, Night is a starry blue.
Key saved. It is stored encrypted on this phone.
Only needed for Ask AI. The key is encrypted with your phone\'s secure storage and never shown, logged or exported. You pay your AI provider directly; Mycelium never sees your bill.

Plays five made-up apps for about 100 seconds. Demo rows are marked and hidden again when the demo stops.
Read-only questions to the database, for example counting events. Only SELECT works; nothing can be changed here.
Fills the garden with made-up activity so you can see how Mycelium looks without waiting. A red banner shows while it plays.

string-array.name: help_howto_a
string-array.item: Open My Apps, tick the apps, tap Save, then tap the status chip at the top and Start protection.
Open Insights, Garden. Under an app, find the tracker and tap Block. Tap Unblock to undo.
Add your own key in Settings. In Ask the Gardener turn on Ask AI. You see what would be sent and choose Send or Cancel.
Open Setup Check and fix anything that is not green, especially battery and Private DNS.

resources.string: Your data is kept and processed on your device.
Every lookup, statistic, alert and Gardener answer is made and kept on this phone. There is no account, no analytics and no server of ours.
Only when you add your own AI key, turn on Ask AI and tap Send: the facts shown in the preview go to the AI provider. Nothing else, ever.
It sees which websites apps look up, not what they send. Apps with their own private DNS, or fixed addresses, can slip past. Data use is counted by Android in blocks of about two hours.
